solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quiet game ultimately inviting dismissive gesture

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of inviting

explanation.surface: Someone asks for silence and a game, and is met with a dismissive wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game ultimately' looks like a unit, but 'game' gives RU (rugby union) and 'ultimately' acts on 'inviting', the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising both shoulders briefly is a common bodily signal of indifference or of not caring.

clue.text: Season very good for trapping black antelope

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the pair before

parts.note: one of the four seasons
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
OK as approval of something good

explanation.surface: A spring season is ideal for catching a dark antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap here is two pieces working together: the season and the approval stand side by side, and the black goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The springbok is a southern African gazelle-like animal, the national emblem of South Africa and its rugby team.

clue.text: Advert displayed in Hampshire ferries

indicators.note: something displayed in a place is on show inside it, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the county name runs into the start of the boats

explanation.surface: An advertisement is put up aboard ferries sailing from Hampshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' reads as a noun, a poster; here it is the rare verb, as in 'to advert to a point'. Hampshire is an English county on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb advert, now formal, means to turn attention to or mention a matter in passing, a sense shared with this word.

clue.text: Dashing young men annoy workers

parts.note: to gall is to irritate
worker ants, the crossword's usual workers

explanation.surface: Flashy young men irritate the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' as ANTS is a standard crossword shortcut, from the worker caste of an ant colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is an old word for a stylish, fashionable young man, often attentive to women.

clue.text: Woman finally delighting in breakfast food, like the governor

parts.note: Vi, short for Violet or Victoria

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a breakfast staple

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of delighting

explanation.surface: A woman enjoys her breakfast cereal, just as the governor does.
explanation.walkthrough: Vi is a common crossword woman, short for Violet. 'Delighting in' reads as enjoyment, but 'in' is the instruction to insert.
explanation.definitionFit: A viceroy or governor rules on behalf of a monarch, so anything pertaining to that office is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Huge area included in visits regularly

indicators.note: to be included in is to be placed within, so one piece sits inside another
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A huge area is taken in on regular visits.
explanation.walkthrough: A sits inside VST, the odd letters of 'visits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size or extent, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Maritime force's phantom provider of credit, might Spooner have said?

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: a phantom is a ghost and a credit card provides credit; swapping their opening sounds gives the answer

explanation.surface: A navy has a ghostly bank card, or so the reverend might have put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the G and C sounds of GHOST CARD. The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the service that patrols a nation's shores, rescues people at sea and guards against smuggling.

clue.text: Refuge in holiday location, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something turned to for help
second meaning: a place people go on holiday, such as a seaside town

explanation.surface: Someone takes shelter at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the holiday location as one kind of the second meaning, not the only one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a source of help one falls back on, and also a town or complex visited for leisure.

clue.text: Be drawn to fireplace, embracing Sackville-West

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: the metal frame holding a fire
Vita Sackville-West, the English writer and garden designer

explanation.surface: People are drawn to the fire, cosying up to a famous writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Vita Sackville-West was an English poet and novelist who created the gardens at Sissinghurst.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pulled towards something, as if by an attracting force, is the figurative sense of this verb.

clue.text: Relaxing, retailing pork pies

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stretched out, at rest
second meaning: telling untruths, since pork pies is rhyming slang for lies and to retail a story is to recount it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retailing pork pies' sounds like a butcher's trade; 'pork pies' is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, and 'retail' means to pass on a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both reclining at ease on a bed or sofa and the act of telling falsehoods.

clue.text: Draws principally involving a plant in Asia

parts.note: a raffle is a prize draw

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first of all, so the leading letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Lotteries mainly concern a plant grown in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws' looks like a verb but is the plural noun, prize draws.
explanation.definitionFit: This parasitic Southeast Asian plant, named after Stamford Raffles, produces the world's largest single flower.

clue.text: Guru took to the water alongside island

parts.note: past tense of swim
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher went swimming beside an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alongside' simply places the two pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism a swami is a religious teacher or holy man, much as a guru is a spiritual guide.

clue.text: Fellow originally residing in Donne's island?

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: John Donne wrote 'No man is an island', so his island is no man

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of residing

explanation.surface: A man who first lived on the poet's island.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: John Donne wrote 'No man is an island', so his island is taken to be 'no man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name serves as an example of a fellow, a chap; Norman is one such name.

clue.text: Scottish city's currency recognised by auditors

indicators.note: auditors are literally listeners, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: sterling is the British currency

explanation.surface: Auditors check a Scottish city's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' suggests accountants, but here they are simply people listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirling is a historic city in central Scotland, famous for its castle and the Wallace Monument.

clue.text: Capital initially invested in urchin's discharge

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: an urchin is a brat, and the possessive keeps the S

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of invested
what a volcano discharges

explanation.surface: Money is first put into a street child's emissions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money for investing; it is the definition. 'Initially invested' gives just I, which goes inside BRAT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Bratislava is the capital city of Slovakia, on the Danube.

clue.text: Lively new routes to east of French wood

parts.note: bois is French for wood

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Exciting new paths lead east from a French forest.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'to east of' puts the rearranged letters to the right of BOIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe noisy, energetic, high-spirited behaviour, a close synonym.

clue.text: Guilelessness of civil engineer in pub in past times

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: once means formerly
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer's naivety, drinking in a pub in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two 'in's: the first inserts the engineer, the second simply joins pub and past times into one string.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilelessness is a lack of cunning or deceit, the naive purity that this noun also names.

clue.text: Set about a Highland Scot

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: jelly sets, or gels
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fixes on a man from the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' could be many things; here it is the verb meaning to solidify.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Celt, especially from the Scottish Highlands and islands.

clue.text: Dawn entertaining male priest in glare of publicity

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: first light is dawn
M is the abbreviation for male
Eli, the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: Dawn is hosting a male priest who is now in the media spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name; it is daybreak. ELI is the crossword's favourite priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Limelight was once used for stage lighting, so being in it now means being the focus of public attention.

clue.text: Poisonous substance manufactured in a European port

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw material, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written

explanation.surface: A toxin is produced in a harbour city in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade, also used medically to dilate the pupils.

clue.text: English landscape gardener known north of the border

definitions.meaning: first meaning: William, the 18th-century designer of the gardens at Stowe and Rousham
second meaning: the Scots past participle of ken, to know

explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland, where ken means know; this form is its past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a famous Georgian garden designer and is also Scottish dialect for something known.

clue.text: Heavenly phenomenon recognised at first in celebrity's squad

parts.note: a celebrity is a star, and the possessive keeps the S

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a squad is a team

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of recognised

explanation.surface: A celestial event is spotted early by a celebrity's entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on 'celebrity's' is kept as a letter rather than read as grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers use the term for a group of stars moving together through the galaxy, a feature of the sky.

clue.text: Hospital worker, possibly, left with little sign of hesitation

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
er is the small sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A hospital employee leaves, slightly unsure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the past tense of leave; it is the nautical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals employ staff to move patients and equipment around; that is one example of the job, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Sport the French must carry over

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: le is French for the
to go over something is to go across it

explanation.surface: The French are obliged to carry some game over the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry over' looks like one phrase; 'over' is the piece being carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks, originating with Indigenous peoples of North America.

clue.text: Neglected state of bachelor in big car

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: a limo, or limousine, is a large luxury car
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees

explanation.surface: A single man ends up forgotten, sitting in a limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: B for bachelor comes from university degrees such as BA and BSc.
explanation.definitionFit: A project left in limbo is stuck in an uncertain, ignored condition with no progress or decision.

clue.text: Deadly human being!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: causing death, as in a fatal wound
second meaning: a person, as one who must die

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes it read like a verdict on someone dangerous; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a fatal wound or enemy, and the noun names a person subject to death.

clue.text: Work hard on back of durable fabric

parts.note: to toil is to labour

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of durable

explanation.surface: Someone labours over hard-wearing cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Durable fabric' looks like the definition, but 'durable' gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a light cotton or linen cloth, also used for patterned prints and dressmakers' trial garments.

clue.text: A coconut stall, pale greyish in colour

parts.note: taken as written
a coconut shy is a fairground stall

explanation.surface: A fairground stall painted a washed-out grey.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground game where you throw balls to knock coconuts off stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Something the colour of ash from a fire is pale and grey, which is exactly what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Painter working in US opera house?

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: the Met, New York's Metropolitan Opera
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An artist has a job at an American opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface is fanciful: the painter never worked at the Met.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist famous for his water lilies, a classic example of a painter.

clue.text: Seaman doing what seamen do, we hear — making a sharp descent?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: hearing deals in sound alone, so a spelling that is merely pronounced the same way is wanted

parts.note: sailors sail

explanation.surface: A sailor is busy doing sailorly things, taking a steep plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a playful description: descending a cliff on a rope is steep, not quite a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: This sport involves lowering oneself down a vertical rock face or wall on a fixed rope.

clue.text: Old archdeacon given money prepared in advance

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: An elderly churchman receives cash set aside beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England an archdeacon's title is 'the Venerable', shortened to Ven. 'The ready' is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Food sold this way has been pre-prepared so it only needs cooking, hence made up beforehand.

clue.text: Leave former partner to take courses

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
taking the courses of a meal is eating

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their ex to go off and study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a verb; it is the noun, permission to be away. 'Courses' are dishes of a meal, not classes.
explanation.definitionFit: At British schools and colleges this Latin term is formal permission for temporary absence.
